newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts $430 mln trade gap so far in July.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts $430 mln trade gap so far in July.

text.p: Brazil posted a trade deficit of $430 million in the period July 1-27, with exports of $4.415 billion and imports of $4.845 billion, a senior Finance Ministry official said Tuesday.
Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, the ministry's economic policy secretary, said that in the fourth week of July exports amounted to $1.176 billion and imports to $1.373 billion.
In a statement, the Finance and Industry and Commerce ministries said average daily exports so far in July stood at $232.4 million, while average daily imports were $255 million.
In the last week, average daily exports rose to $235.2 million from $230.8 million the previous week, and average daily imports hit $274.6 million, against $262.6 million the week before.
If maintained until the end of the month, July's trade gap would take the trade deficit for the first seven months of the year to over $5.0 billion.
